functionalObligations.text: a depositor's liquidity-pool token is staked by the protocol into the corresponding external gauge and credited one-for-one into a per-pool reward contract, withdrawable at any time with no deposit or withdrawal fee
functionalObligations.note: Sh is approximate: the receipt is one-for-one rather than a varying pro-rata ratio, the degenerate case of a proportional pool claim. Rd is a DEPARTURE from the corpus, which omits it: the unconditional par withdrawal right is the whole difference between this deposit path and the CRV path in F5. Live Booster.poolLength() = 580.

functionalObligations.text: the external gauge's emissions token, the protocol's own token and arbitrary third-party reward tokens accrue to the staker by a per-token reward-per-share index
each harvest's rewards are paid out linearly over a rolling one-week period rather than at once
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus omits Sr for Convex. The reward contracts stream a rate over a fixed duration, which is what Sr names.

functionalObligations.text: the reward rate on every pooled deposit is multiplied by a boost derived from the protocol's share of a different token's escrowed supply, held by the protocol rather than by the depositor, up to a hard multiple of two and a half
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. working_balance = min(l, 0.4*l + 0.6*L*V/V_total). Neither Sh nor Ix can express a claim whose accrual rate depends on an external, transferable, pooled quantity held by a third party. This is the mechanism that makes aggregation rational — Convex's entire economic reason to exist — and it has no name.

functionalObligations.text: the governance token of the upstream protocol, when deposited, is added to a single permanent escrow position from which no party can ever withdraw it
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Rd explicitly does NOT apply: the structured ABSENCE of a redemption right is the design. Live 2026-08-04: veCRV.balanceOf(0x989AEb4d175e16225E39E87d0D97A3360524AD80) = 420,633,657.30 of a 783,593,117.83 total supply, 53.68%; locked__end = 2030-07-25.

functionalObligations.text: that escrow is re-extended toward its maximum term by any permissionless deposit call whenever it would otherwise begin to decay
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. MAXTIME = 4*364 days and _lockCurve() calls increaseTime whenever the week-rounded target exceeds the stored unlock, so the commitment renews itself forever without any governance act. No symbol names a self-renewing commitment.

functionalObligations.text: in exchange the depositor receives a transferable token whose only exit is sale on a secondary market, since the position behind it has no redemption function
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A liquid wrapper of a permanently locked position, whose peg is a market rather than a redemption. This pattern — liquid staking, liquid restaking, liquid lockers — is one of the most replicated in DeFi and there is no symbol for it.

functionalObligations.text: holders of that wrapper receive the upstream protocol's admin fees and may elect any mix between receiving them in the fee asset and receiving the two governance tokens
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd). CORRECTION to the corpus, which describes this as 3CRV revenue: admin fees now arrive as crvUSD. The depositor's election between a cash asset and a governance asset is not named by Fd and is a second instance of the elective-return pattern seen at Huma 2.0.

functionalObligations.text: voting weight over the escrowed position is non-transferable and is a function of the time remaining on a lock
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the largest single residue finding in this lane by TVL. Ep names a period boundary; Tg names a delay before execution; neither names a weight that is a function of time remaining. The corpus emits Ve here on contested-register grounds, calling it the strongest such case in its lane. Ve is not among the 58, so this construction does not emit it — with the consequence the corpus itself anticipated: strip the vote layer and what remains (Sh + Ix + Sr + Em) is indistinguishable from any staking-rewards contract.

functionalObligations.text: the protocol's own token can be locked for a sixteen-week minimum to obtain a governance weight measured at weekly epoch boundaries
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call lockDuration() = 9,676,800, epochCount() = 232, lockedSupply() = 46,056,535.73 on 0x72a19342e8F1838460eBFCCEf09F6585e32db86E, accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, corpus marker retained: Ep means an epoch-GATED TRANSITION and here the epochs gate voting weight and reward eligibility rather than a state transition. CORRECTION to the corpus marker's text: vote-lock epochs are weekly (Thursday 00:00 UTC) but the upstream gauge-weight vote is BI-weekly (Thursday 00:00 to Tuesday 00:00).

functionalObligations.text: lock-holders vote in a proposal on this protocol whose weights are anchored to a historical epoch balance, and a separate executor contract later casts the aggregated result into the foreign protocol's gauge controller through a registered surrogate
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two votes at different addresses with different electorates, joined by a surrogate registry and a one-level delegation. NEW MECHANISM the corpus does not carry: convex-eth/voting was created 2026-04-15 and is live — Booster.voteDelegate() = 0x5349fFbA494Ac3C888ffA16Fd438f44b8C67fb07, exactly the VoteDelegateExtension in that repo's deployment/mainnet.json. Any decomposition reading only convex-eth/platform describes Convex as it was in 2025.

functionalObligations.text: the protocol acquires and exercises governance rights inside four foreign protocols that it does not control
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Au covers an execution scope granted by a principal over its own assets; nothing covers acquiring voting rights in a system you are not part of and renting them out. Related boundary finding: no Convex contract implements a vote-incentive market — a code search over convex-eth/platform returns one body-less interface and one test script, and convex-eth/voting returns zero. The bribe market exists (Votium) but is a separate protocol with no shared addresses, so the corpus's residue item 'no element for a bribe market' should be re-scoped as a boundary finding rather than a missing element of Convex.

functionalObligations.text: seventeen per cent of all harvested emissions revenue is taken and split ten to wrapper-stakers, four and a half to lock-holders and two to the treasury, each component bounded in code and the total capped at twenty per cent
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), promoted from a corpus marker. CORRECTION: the widely quoted 16% with a 10/5/1 split is outdated; live Booster values are lockIncentive 1000, stakerIncentive 450, earmarkIncentive 50, platformFee 200 against MaxFees 2000.

functionalObligations.text: half a per cent of that revenue is paid to whichever anonymous address calls the harvest function
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Fd names distribution of surplus to claimants; this is a subsidy for liveness, paid to a stranger for performing work the protocol cannot perform for itself. The same object appears at CIAN and Huma as an unpaid keeper dependency, which makes the paid version the interesting control.

functionalObligations.text: the protocol's own token is minted to depositors in proportion to harvested revenue, on a schedule whose multiplier steps down with cumulative supply and reaches zero at a hard cap
functionalObligations.note: CORRECTION the corpus does not carry and stage 1 asked to be checked: the mechanism is in code but numerically dead. Live totalSupply() = 99,983,304.90 of a 100,000,000 cap, i.e. cliff 999 of 1000 and a multiplier of 0.001, zero at the next cliff. Em is retained because this obligation exists and only Em discharges it, but it must NOT be treated as a source of return: the corpus's canonicalForm lists Em as load-bearing and a construction that explains Convex's economics through it reproduces a protocol that no longer exists.

functionalObligations.text: arbitrary third-party reward tokens attached to an upstream gauge are forwarded through per-pool stash contracts and virtual-balance children whose balances mirror the parent pool without holding its assets
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A pass-through claim on an unknown future token set, accounted by mirroring another contract's balances. No symbol names a shadow-balance accounting adapter.

functionalObligations.text: the owner may shut the entire system, pulling every deposited position out of the external gauges and marking every pool closed, and may shut individual pools
no deployed contract's code can be replaced: the protocol commits to immutability and offers shutdown-and-redeploy as its only migration path
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the second correction stage 1 asked to be checked. The corpus emits Up and Tg for Convex; both are REFUTED. Blockscout reports proxy = None on Booster, VoterProxy, CVX, cvxCRV, CrvDepositor and CvxLockerV2, and no timelock is documented or found anywhere in the system. Immutability plus a kill switch is a materially different risk object from an upgradeable proxy and must not decompose to the same symbols. The residue is structural: the vocabulary can name mutability (Up) and delay (Tg) but has no way to ASSERT their absence, so a protocol that has bound itself and one that simply has not been audited for it are indistinguishable.
